rows.question: What is one way that RF energy can affect human body tissue?
rows.answer_c: It causes the blood count to reach a dangerously low level

rows.question: Which of the following is used to determine RF exposure from a transmitted signal?
rows.answer_c: Its power density

rows.question: How can you determine that your station complies with FCC RF exposure regulations?
rows.answer_a: By calculation based on FCC OET Bulletin 65
rows.answer_b: By calculation based on computer modeling
rows.answer_c: By measurement of field strength using calibrated equipment

rows.question: What does “time averaging” mean when evaluating RF radiation exposure?
rows.answer_a: The average amount of power developed by the transmitter over a specific 24-hour period
rows.answer_b: The average time it takes RF radiation to have any long-term effect on the body
rows.answer_c: The total time of the exposure
rows.answer_d: The total RF exposure averaged over a certain period

rows.question: What must you do if an evaluation of your station shows that the RF energy radiated by your station exceeds permissible limits for possible human absorption?
rows.answer_a: Take action to prevent human exposure to the excessive RF fields
rows.answer_b: File an Environmental Impact Statement (EIS-97) with the FCC
rows.answer_c: Secure written permission from your neighbors to operate above the controlled MPE limits

rows.question: What must you do if your station fails to meet the FCC RF exposure exemption criteria?
rows.answer_a: Perform an RF exposure evaluation in accordance with FCC OET Bulletin 65
rows.answer_b: Contact the FCC for permission to transmit
rows.answer_c: Perform an RF exposure evaluation in accordance with World Meteorological Organization guidelines

rows.question: What is the effect of modulation duty cycle on RF exposure?
rows.answer_a: A lower duty cycle permits greater power levels to be transmitted
rows.answer_b: A higher duty cycle permits greater power levels to be transmitted
rows.answer_c: Low duty cycle transmitters are exempt from RF exposure evaluation requirements
rows.answer_d: High duty cycle transmitters are exempt from RF exposure requirements

rows.question: Which of the following steps must an amateur operator take to ensure compliance with RF safety regulations?
rows.answer_a: Post a copy of FCC Part 97.13 in the station
rows.answer_b: Notify neighbors within a 100-foot radius of the antenna of the existence of the station and power levels
rows.answer_c: Perform a routine RF exposure evaluation and prevent access to any identified high exposure areas

rows.question: What type of instrument can be used to accurately measure an RF field strength?
rows.answer_a: A receiver with digital signal processing (DSP) noise reduction
rows.answer_b: A calibrated field strength meter with a calibrated antenna
rows.answer_c: An SWR meter with a peak-reading function
rows.answer_d: An oscilloscope with a high-stability crystal marker generator

rows.question: What should be done if evaluation shows that a neighbor might experience more than the allowable limit of RF exposure from the main lobe of a directional antenna?
rows.answer_a: Change to a non-polarized antenna with higher gain
rows.answer_b: Use an antenna with a higher front-to-back ratio
rows.answer_c: Take precautions to ensure that the antenna cannot be pointed in their direction when they are present

rows.question: What precaution should be taken if you install an indoor transmitting antenna?
rows.answer_a: Locate the antenna close to your operating position to minimize feed-line radiation
rows.answer_b: Position the antenna along the edge of a wall to reduce parasitic radiation
rows.answer_c: Make sure that MPE limits are not exceeded in occupied areas
rows.answer_d: Make sure the antenna is properly shielded

rows.question: What stations are subject to the FCC rules on RF exposure?
rows.answer_a: All commercial stations; amateur radio stations are exempt
rows.answer_b: Only stations with antennas lower than one wavelength above the ground
rows.answer_c: Only stations transmitting more than 500 watts PEP
rows.answer_d: All stations with a time-averaged transmission of more than one milliwatt

rows.question: Which wire or wires in a four-conductor 240 VAC circuit should be attached to fuses or circuit breakers?
rows.answer_c: Only the ground wire

rows.question: According to the National Electrical Code, what is the minimum wire size that may be used safely for wiring with a 20-ampere circuit breaker?
rows.answer_c: AWG number 12

rows.question: Which size of fuse or circuit breaker would be appropriate to use with a circuit that uses AWG number 14 wiring?
rows.answer_c: 20 amperes

rows.question: Where should the station’s lightning protection ground system be located?
rows.answer_a: As close to the station equipment as possible
rows.answer_c: Next to the closest power pole
rows.answer_d: Parallel to the water supply line

rows.question: Which of the following conditions will cause a ground fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) to disconnect AC power?
rows.answer_a: Current flowing from one or more of the hot wires to the neutral wire
rows.answer_b: Current flowing from one or more of the hot wires directly to ground
rows.answer_c: Overvoltage on the hot wires

rows.question: Which of the following is covered by the National Electrical Code?
rows.answer_c: Electrical safety of the station
rows.answer_d: RF exposure limits of the human body

rows.question: Which of these choices should be observed when climbing a tower using a safety harness?
rows.answer_a: Always hold on to the tower with one hand
rows.answer_b: Confirm that the harness is rated for the weight of the climber and that it is within its allowable service life
rows.answer_c: Ensure that all heavy tools are securely fastened to the harness

rows.question: What should be done before climbing a tower that supports electrically powered devices?
rows.answer_a: Notify the electric company that a person will be working on the tower
rows.answer_b: Make sure all circuits that supply power to the tower are locked out and tagged
rows.answer_c: Unground the base of the tower

rows.question: Which of the following is true of an emergency generator installation?
rows.answer_a: The generator should be operated in a well-ventilated area
rows.answer_b: The generator must be insulated from ground
rows.answer_c: Fuel should be stored near the generator for rapid refueling in case of an emergency

rows.question: Which of the following is a danger from lead-tin solder?
rows.answer_a: Lead can contaminate food if hands are not washed carefully after handling the solder
rows.answer_b: High voltages can cause lead-tin solder to disintegrate suddenly
rows.answer_c: Tin in the solder can “cold flow,” causing shorts in the circuit
rows.answer_d: RF energy can convert the lead into a poisonous gas

rows.question: Which of the following is required for lightning protection ground rods?
rows.answer_a: They must be bonded to all buried water and gas lines
rows.answer_b: Bends in ground wires must be made as close as possible to a right angle
rows.answer_c: Lightning grounds must be connected to all ungrounded wiring
rows.answer_d: They must be bonded together with all other grounds

rows.question: What is the purpose of a power supply interlock?
rows.answer_a: To prevent unauthorized changes to the circuit that would void the manufacturer’s warranty
rows.answer_b: To shut down the unit if it becomes too hot
rows.answer_c: To ensure that dangerous voltages are removed if the cabinet is opened
rows.answer_d: To shut off the power supply if too much voltage is produced

rows.question: Where should lightning arrestors be located?
rows.answer_a: Where the feed lines enter the building
rows.answer_b: On the antenna, opposite the feed point
rows.answer_c: In series with each ground lead
rows.answer_d: At the closest power pole ground electrode

rows.question: On which HF and/or MF amateur bands are there portions where General class licensees cannot transmit?
rows.answer_c: 80 meters, 40 meters, 20 meters, and 15 meters

rows.question: On which of the following bands is phone operation prohibited?
rows.answer_c: 17 meters

rows.question: On which of the following bands is image transmission prohibited?
rows.answer_c: 20 meters

rows.question: On which of the following frequencies are General class licensees prohibited from operating as control operator?
rows.answer_c: 21.275 MHz to 21.300 MHz

rows.question: Which of the following applies when the FCC rules designate the amateur service as a secondary user on a band?
rows.answer_a: Amateur stations must record the call sign of the primary service station before operating on a frequency assigned to that station
rows.answer_b: Amateur stations may use the band only during emergencies
rows.answer_c: Amateur stations must not cause harmful interference to primary users and must accept interference from primary users
rows.answer_d: Amateur stations may only operate during specific hours of the day, while primary users are permitted 24-hour use of the band

rows.question: On which amateur frequencies in the 10-meter band may stations with a General class control operator transmit CW emissions?
rows.answer_c: 28.025 MHz to 28.300 MHz only

rows.question: Which HF bands have segments exclusively allocated to Amateur Extra licensees?
rows.answer_c: All HF bands except 160 meters and 10 meters

rows.question: Which of the following frequencies is within the General class portion of the 15-meter band?
What portion of the 10-meter band is available for repeater use?
rows.answer_b: The portion between 28.1 MHz and 28.2 MHz
rows.answer_c: The portion between 28.3 MHz and 28.5 MHz

rows.question: When General class licensees are not permitted to use the entire voice portion of a band, which portion of the voice segment is available to them?
rows.answer_c: The lower frequency portion on frequencies below 7.3 MHz, and the upper portion on frequencies above 14.150 MHz
rows.answer_d: The upper frequency portion on frequencies below 7.3 MHz, and the lower portion on frequencies above 14.150 MHz

rows.question: What is the maximum height above ground for an antenna structure not near a public use airport without requiring notification to the FAA and registration with the FCC?
rows.answer_c: 200 feet

rows.question: With which of the following conditions must beacon stations comply?
rows.answer_a: No more than one beacon station may transmit in the same band from the same station location
rows.answer_b: The frequency must be coordinated with the National Beacon Organization
rows.answer_c: The frequency must be posted on the internet or published in a national periodical

rows.question: Which of the following is a purpose of a beacon station as identified in the FCC rules?
rows.answer_c: Transmission of bulletins of general interest to amateur radio licensees

rows.question: Which of the following transmissions is permitted for all amateur stations?
rows.answer_a: Unidentified transmissions of less than 10 seconds duration for test purposes only
rows.answer_b: Automatic retransmission of other amateur signals by any amateur station
rows.answer_c: Occasional retransmission of weather and propagation forecast information from US government stations
rows.answer_d: Encrypted messages, if not intended to facilitate a criminal act

rows.question: Which of the following one-way transmissions are permitted?
rows.answer_a: Unidentified test transmissions of less than 10 seconds in duration
rows.answer_b: Transmissions to assist with learning the International Morse code
rows.answer_c: Regular transmissions offering equipment for sale, if intended for amateur radio use

rows.question: Under what conditions are state and local governments permitted to regulate amateur radio antenna structures?
rows.answer_a: Under no circumstances, FCC rules take priority
rows.answer_b: At any time and to any extent necessary to accomplish a legitimate purpose of the state or local entity, provided that proper filings are made with the FCC
rows.answer_c: Only when such structures exceed 50 feet in height and are clearly visible 1,000 feet from the structure
rows.answer_d: Amateur Service communications must be reasonably accommodated, and regulations must constitute the minimum practical to accommodate a legitimate purpose of the state or local entity

rows.question: What are the restrictions on the use of abbreviations or procedural signals in the amateur service?
rows.answer_b: They may be used if they do not obscure the meaning of a message
rows.answer_c: They are not permitted
rows.answer_d: They are limited to those expressly listed in Part 97 of the FCC rules

rows.question: When is it permissible to communicate with amateur stations in countries outside the areas administered by the Federal Communications Commission?
rows.answer_a: Only when the foreign country has a formal third-party agreement filed with the FCC
rows.answer_b: When the contact is with amateurs in any country except those whose administrations have notified the ITU that they object to such communications
rows.answer_c: Only when the contact is with amateurs licensed by a country which is a member of the United Nations, or by a territory possessed by such a country
rows.answer_d: Only when the contact is with amateurs licensed by a country which is a member of the International Amateur Radio Union, or by a territory possessed by such a country

rows.question: On what HF frequencies are automatically controlled beacons permitted?
rows.answer_a: On any frequency if power is less than 1 watt
rows.answer_b: On any frequency if transmissions are in Morse code
rows.answer_c: 21.08 MHz to 21.09 MHz

rows.question: What is the power limit for beacon stations?
rows.answer_c: 100 watts PEP output

rows.question: Who or what determines “good engineering and good amateur practice,” as applied to the operation of an amateur station in all respects not covered by the Part 97 rules?
rows.answer_c: The IEEE

rows.question: What is the maximum transmitter power an amateur station may use on 10.140 MHz?
rows.answer_c: 1500 watts PEP output

rows.question: What is the maximum transmitter power an amateur station may use on the 12-meter band?
rows.answer_c: 1500 watts PEP output
rows.answer_d: An effective radiated power equivalent to 100 watts from a half-wave dipole

rows.question: What is the maximum bandwidth permitted by FCC rules for amateur radio stations transmitting on USB frequencies in the 60-meter band?
rows.answer_c: 1.8 kHz

rows.question: Which of the following is required by the FCC rules when operating in the 60-meter band?
rows.answer_a: If you are using an antenna other than a dipole, you must keep a record of the gain of your antenna
rows.answer_b: You must keep a record of the date, time, frequency, power level, and stations worked
rows.answer_c: You must keep a record of all third-party traffic
rows.answer_d: You must keep a record of the manufacturer of your equipment and the antenna used

rows.question: What is the limit for transmitter power on the 28 MHz band for a General Class control operator?
rows.answer_c: 1500 watts PEP output

rows.question: What is the limit for transmitter power on the 1.8 MHz band?
rows.answer_c: 1200 watts PEP output

rows.question: What must be done before using a new digital protocol on the air?
rows.answer_b: Obtain an experimental license from the FCC
rows.answer_c: Publicly document the technical characteristics of the protocol
rows.answer_d: Submit a rule-making proposal to the FCC describing the codes and methods of the technique

rows.question: What measurement is specified by FCC rules that regulate maximum power?
rows.answer_c: PEP input to the antenna

rows.question: Who may receive partial credit for the elements represented by an expired amateur radio license?
rows.answer_a: Any person who can demonstrate that they once held an FCC-issued General, Advanced, or Amateur Extra class license that was not revoked by the FCC
rows.answer_b: Anyone who held an FCC-issued amateur radio license that expired not less than 5 and not more than 15 years ago
rows.answer_c: Any person who previously held an amateur license issued by another country, but only if that country has a current reciprocal licensing agreement with the FCC
rows.answer_d: Only persons who once held an FCC issued Novice, Technician, or Technician Plus license

rows.question: What license examinations may you administer as an accredited Volunteer Examiner holding a General class operator license?
rows.answer_b: None, only Amateur Extra class licensees may be accredited
rows.answer_c: Technician only

rows.question: On which of the following band segments may you operate if you are a Technician class operator and have an unexpired Certificate of Successful Completion of Examination (CSCE) for General class privileges?
rows.answer_a: Only the Technician band segments until your upgrade is posted in the FCC database
rows.answer_b: Only on the Technician band segments until you have a receipt for the FCC application fee payment
rows.answer_c: On any General or Technician class band segment
rows.answer_d: On any General or Technician class band segment except 30 meters and 60 meters

rows.question: Who must observe the administration of a Technician class license examination?
rows.answer_a: At least three Volunteer Examiners of General class or higher
rows.answer_b: At least two Volunteer Examiners of General class or higher
rows.answer_c: At least two Volunteer Examiners of Technician class or higher
rows.answer_d: At least three Volunteer Examiners of Technician class

rows.question: When operating a US station by remote control from outside the country, what license is required of the control operator?
rows.answer_b: Only an appropriate US operator/primary license and a special remote station permit from the FCC
rows.answer_c: Only a license from the foreign country, as long as the call sign includes identification of portable operation in the US
rows.answer_d: A license from the foreign country and a special remote station permit from the FCC

rows.question: Until an upgrade to General class is shown in the FCC database, when must a Technician licensee identify with “AG” after their call sign?
rows.answer_a: Whenever they operate using General class frequency privileges
rows.answer_b: Whenever they operate on any amateur frequency
rows.answer_c: Whenever they operate using Technician frequency privileges
rows.answer_d: A special identifier is not required if their General class license application has been filed with the FCC

rows.question: Volunteer Examiners are accredited by what organization?
rows.answer_c: A Volunteer Examiner Coordinator

rows.question: Which of the following criteria must be met for a non-US citizen to be an accredited Volunteer Examiner?
rows.answer_a: The person must be a resident of the US for a minimum of 5 years
rows.answer_b: The person must hold an FCC granted amateur radio license of General class or above
rows.answer_c: The person’s home citizenship must be in ITU region 2
rows.answer_d: None of these choices is correct; a non-US citizen cannot be a Volunteer Examiner

rows.question: How long is a Certificate of Successful Completion of Examination (CSCE) valid for exam element credit?
rows.answer_c: 365 days
rows.answer_d: For as long as your current license is valid

rows.question: What is the minimum age that one must be to qualify as an accredited Volunteer Examiner?
rows.answer_c: 21 years

rows.question: What action is required to obtain a new General class license after a previously held license has expired and the two-year grace period has passed?
rows.answer_a: They must have a letter from the FCC showing they once held an amateur or commercial license
rows.answer_b: There are no requirements other than being able to show a copy of the expired license
rows.answer_c: Contact the FCC to have the license reinstated
rows.answer_d: The applicant must show proof of the appropriate expired license grant and pass the current Element 2 exam

rows.question: When operating a station in South America by remote control over the internet from the US, what regulations apply?
rows.answer_a: Those of both the remote station’s country and the FCC
rows.answer_b: Those of the remote station’s country and the FCC’s third-party regulations
rows.answer_c: Only those of the remote station’s country

rows.question: Which of the following would disqualify a third party from participating in sending a message via an amateur station?
rows.answer_a: The third party’s amateur license has been revoked and not reinstated
rows.answer_b: The third party is not a US citizen
rows.answer_c: The third party is speaking in a language other than English

rows.question: When may a 10-meter repeater retransmit the 2-meter signal from a station that has a Technician class control operator?
rows.answer_b: Only if the station on 10-meters is operating under a Special Temporary Authorization allowing such retransmission
rows.answer_c: Only during an FCC-declared general state of communications emergency
rows.answer_d: Only if the 10-meter repeater control operator holds at least a General class license

rows.question: What is required to conduct communications with a digital station operating under automatic control outside the automatic control band segments?
rows.answer_a: The station initiating the contact must be under local or remote control
rows.answer_b: The interrogating transmission must be made by another automatically controlled station
rows.answer_c: No third-party traffic may be transmitted
rows.answer_d: The control operator of the interrogating station must hold an Amateur Extra class license

rows.question: Which of the following conditions require a licensed amateur radio operator to take specific steps to avoid harmful interference to other users or facilities?
rows.answer_a: When operating within one mile of an FCC Monitoring Station
rows.answer_b: When using a band where the Amateur Service is secondary
rows.answer_c: When a station is transmitting spread spectrum emissions

rows.question: What are the restrictions on messages sent to a third party in a country with which there is a Third-Party Agreement?
rows.answer_a: They must relate to emergencies or disaster relief
rows.answer_b: They must be for other licensed amateurs
rows.answer_c: They must relate to amateur radio, or remarks of a personal character, or messages relating to emergencies or disaster relief
rows.answer_d: The message must be limited to no longer than 1 minute in duration and the name of the third party must be recorded in the station log

rows.question: The frequency allocations of which ITU region apply to radio amateurs operating in North and South America?
rows.answer_c: Region 2

rows.question: In what part of the 2.4 GHz band may an amateur station communicate with non-licensed Wi-Fi stations?
rows.answer_c: Channels 42 through 45

rows.question: What is the maximum PEP output allowed for spread spectrum transmissions?
rows.answer_c: 100 watts

rows.question: Why should an amateur operator normally avoid transmitting on 14.100, 18.110, 21.150, 24.930 and 28.200 MHz?
rows.answer_a: A system of propagation beacon stations operates on those frequencies
rows.answer_b: A system of automatic digital stations operates on those frequencies
rows.answer_c: These frequencies are set aside for emergency operations
rows.answer_d: These frequencies are set aside for bulletins from the FCC

rows.question: On what bands may automatically controlled stations transmitting RTTY or data emissions communicate with other automatically controlled digital stations?
rows.answer_a: On any band segment where digital operation is permitted
rows.answer_b: Anywhere in the non-phone segments of the 10-meter or shorter wavelength bands
rows.answer_c: Only in the non-phone Extra Class segments of the bands
rows.answer_d: Anywhere in the 6-meter or shorter wavelength bands, and in limited segments of some of the HF bands

rows.question: When may third-party messages be transmitted via remote control?
rows.answer_a: Under any circumstances in which third party messages are permitted by FCC rules
rows.answer_b: Under no circumstances except for emergencies
rows.answer_c: Only when the message is intended for licensed radio amateurs
rows.answer_d: Only when the message is intended for third parties in areas where licensing is controlled by the FCC

rows.question: Which mode is most commonly used for voice communications on frequencies of 14 MHz or higher?
rows.answer_c: Suppressed sideband

rows.question: Which mode is most commonly used for voice communications on the 160-, 75-, and 40-meter bands?
rows.answer_c: Suppressed sideband

rows.question: Which mode is most commonly used for SSB voice communications in the VHF and UHF bands?
rows.answer_c: Suppressed sideband

rows.question: Which mode is most commonly used for voice communications on the 17- and 12-meter bands?
rows.answer_c: Suppressed sideband

rows.question: Which mode of voice communication is most commonly used on the HF amateur bands?
rows.answer_c: Single sideband

rows.question: Which of the following is an advantage of using single sideband, as compared to other analog voice modes on the HF amateur bands?
rows.answer_b: Less subject to interference from atmospheric static crashes
rows.answer_c: Ease of tuning on receive and immunity to impulse noise
rows.answer_d: Less bandwidth used and greater power efficiency

rows.question: Which of the following statements is true of single sideband (SSB)?
rows.answer_a: Only one sideband and the carrier are transmitted; the other sideband is suppressed
rows.answer_b: Only one sideband is transmitted; the other sideband and carrier are suppressed
rows.answer_c: SSB is the only voice mode authorized on the 20-, 15-, and 10-meter amateur bands
rows.answer_d: SSB is the only voice mode authorized on the 160-, 75-, and 40-meter amateur bands

rows.question: What is the recommended way to break into a phone contact?
rows.answer_a: Say “QRZ” several times, followed by your call sign
rows.answer_c: Say “Breaker Breaker”
rows.answer_d: Say “CQ” followed by the call sign of either station

rows.question: Why do most amateur stations use lower sideband on the 160-, 75-, and 40-meter bands?
rows.answer_a: Lower sideband is more efficient than upper sideband at these frequencies
rows.answer_b: Lower sideband is the only sideband legal on these frequency bands
rows.answer_c: Because it is fully compatible with an AM detector
rows.answer_d: It is commonly accepted amateur practice

rows.question: Which of the following statements is true of VOX operation versus PTT operation?
rows.answer_a: The received signal is more natural sounding
rows.answer_c: It occupies less bandwidth

rows.question: Generally, who should respond to a station in the contiguous 48 states calling “CQ DX”?
rows.answer_a: Any caller is welcome to respond
rows.answer_c: Any stations outside the lower 48 states

rows.question: What control is typically adjusted for proper ALC setting on a single sideband transceiver?
rows.answer_c: Antenna inductance or capacitance

rows.question: Which of the following is true concerning access to frequencies?
rows.answer_c: Except during emergencies, no amateur station has priority access to any frequency
rows.answer_d: Contest operations should yield to non-contest use of frequencies

rows.question: What is the first thing you should do if you are communicating with another amateur station and hear a station in distress break in?
rows.answer_b: Acknowledge the station in distress and determine what assistance may be needed
rows.answer_c: Immediately decrease power to avoid interfering with the station in distress

rows.question: What is good amateur practice if propagation changes during a contact creating interference from other stations using the frequency?
rows.answer_a: Advise the interfering stations that you are on the frequency and that you have priority
rows.answer_b: Decrease power and continue to transmit
rows.answer_c: Attempt to resolve the interference problem with the other stations in a mutually acceptable manner

rows.question: When selecting a CW transmitting frequency, what minimum separation from other stations should be used to minimize interference to stations on adjacent frequencies?
rows.answer_c: 1 kHz to 3 kHz

rows.question: When selecting an SSB transmitting frequency, what minimum separation should be used to minimize interference to stations on adjacent frequencies?
rows.answer_c: 2 kHz to 3 kHz

rows.question: How can you avoid harmful interference on an apparently clear frequency before calling CQ on CW or phone?
rows.answer_a: Send “QRL?” on CW, followed by your call sign; or, if using phone, ask if the frequency is in use, followed by your call sign
rows.answer_b: Listen for 2 minutes before calling CQ
rows.answer_c: Send the letter “V” in Morse code several times and listen for a response, or say “test” several times and listen for a response
rows.answer_d: Send “QSY” on CW or if using phone, announce “the frequency is in use,” then give your call sign and listen for a response

rows.question: Which of the following complies with commonly accepted amateur practice when choosing a frequency on which to initiate a call?
rows.answer_a: Listen on the frequency for at least two minutes to be sure it is clear
rows.answer_b: Identify your station by transmitting your call sign at least 3 times
rows.answer_c: Follow the voluntary band plan

rows.question: What is the voluntary band plan restriction for US stations transmitting within the 48 contiguous states in the 50.1 MHz to 50.125 MHz band segment?
rows.answer_a: Only contacts with stations not within the 48 contiguous states
rows.answer_b: Only contacts with other stations within the 48 contiguous states
rows.answer_c: Only digital contacts

rows.question: Who may be the control operator of an amateur station transmitting in RACES to assist relief operations during a disaster?
rows.answer_a: Only a person holding an FCC-issued amateur operator license
rows.answer_b: Only a RACES net control operator
rows.answer_c: A person holding an FCC-issued amateur operator license or an appropriate government official
rows.answer_d: Any control operator when normal communication systems are operational

rows.question: Which of the following is good amateur practice for net management?
rows.answer_a: Always use multiple sets of phonetics during check-in
rows.answer_b: Have a backup frequency in case of interference or poor conditions
rows.answer_c: Transmit the full net roster at the beginning of every session

rows.question: How often may RACES training drills and tests be routinely conducted without special authorization?
rows.answer_a: No more than 1 hour per month
rows.answer_b: No more than 2 hours per month
rows.answer_c: No more than 1 hour per week
rows.answer_d: No more than 2 hours per week

rows.question: Which of the following describes full break-in CW operation (QSK)?
rows.answer_a: Breaking stations send the Morse code prosign “BK”
rows.answer_b: Automatic keyers, instead of hand keys, are used to send Morse code
rows.answer_c: An operator must activate a manual send/receive switch before and after every transmission
rows.answer_d: Transmitting stations can receive between code characters and elements

rows.question: What should you do if a CW station sends “QRS?”
rows.answer_c: Increase your power

rows.question: What does it mean when a CW operator sends “KN” at the end of a transmission?
rows.answer_c: Listening only for a specific station or stations

rows.question: What does the Q signal “QRL?” mean?
rows.answer_b: “Are you operating full break-in?” or “Can you operate full break-in?”
rows.answer_c: “Are you listening only for a specific station?”
rows.answer_d: “Are you busy?” or “Is this frequency in use?”

rows.question: What is the best speed to use when answering a CQ in Morse code?
rows.answer_a: The fastest speed at which you are comfortable copying, but no slower than the CQ
rows.answer_b: The fastest speed at which you are comfortable copying, but no faster than the CQ
rows.answer_c: At the standard calling speed of 10 wpm
rows.answer_d: At the standard calling speed of 5 wpm

rows.question: What does the term “zero beat” mean in CW operation?
rows.answer_a: Matching the speed of the transmitting station
rows.answer_b: Operating split to avoid interference on frequency
rows.answer_c: Sending without error
rows.answer_d: Matching the transmit frequency to the frequency of a received signal

rows.question: When sending CW, what does a “C” mean when added to the RST report?
rows.answer_b: Report was read from an S meter rather than estimated
rows.answer_c: 100 percent copy

rows.question: What prosign is sent to indicate the end of a formal message when using CW?
rows.answer_c: AR

rows.question: What does the Q signal “QSL” mean?
rows.answer_b: We have already confirmed the contact
rows.answer_c: I have received and understood

rows.question: What does the Q signal “QRN” mean?
rows.answer_c: Zero beat my signal

rows.question: What does the Q signal “QRV” mean?
rows.answer_b: There is interference on the frequency
rows.answer_c: I am quitting for the day

rows.question: What is the Volunteer Monitor Program?
rows.answer_a: Amateur volunteers who are formally enlisted to monitor the airwaves for rules violations
rows.answer_b: Amateur volunteers who conduct amateur licensing examinations
rows.answer_c: Amateur volunteers who conduct frequency coordination for amateur VHF repeaters
rows.answer_d: Amateur volunteers who use their station equipment to help civil defense organizations in times of emergency

rows.question: Which of the following are objectives of the Volunteer Monitor Program?
rows.answer_a: To conduct efficient and orderly amateur licensing examinations
rows.answer_b: To provide emergency and public safety communications
rows.answer_c: To coordinate repeaters for efficient and orderly spectrum usage
rows.answer_d: To encourage amateur radio operators to self-regulate and comply with the rules

rows.question: What procedure may be used by Volunteer Monitors to localize a station whose continuous carrier is holding a repeater on in their area?
rows.answer_a: Compare vertical and horizontal signal strengths on the input frequency
rows.answer_b: Compare beam headings on the repeater input from their home locations with that of other Volunteer Monitors
rows.answer_c: Compare signal strengths between the input and output of the repeater

rows.question: Which of the following describes an azimuthal projection map?
rows.answer_a: A map that shows accurate land masses
rows.answer_b: A map that shows true bearings and distances from a specific location
rows.answer_c: A map that shows the angle at which an amateur satellite crosses the equator
rows.answer_d: A map that shows the number of degrees longitude that an amateur satellite appears to move westward at the equator with each orbit

rows.question: Which of the following indicates that you are looking for an HF contact with any station?
rows.answer_a: Sign your call sign once, followed by the words “listening for a call” -- if no answer, change frequency and repeat
rows.answer_b: Say “QTC” followed by “this is” and your call sign -- if no answer, change frequency and repeat
rows.answer_c: Repeat “CQ” a few times, followed by “this is,” then your call sign a few times, then pause to listen, repeat as necessary
rows.answer_d: Transmit an unmodulated carried for approximately 10 seconds, followed by “this is” and your call sign, and pause to listen -- repeat as necessary

rows.question: How is a directional antenna pointed when making a “long-path” contact with another station?
rows.answer_c: 180 degrees from the station’s short-path heading

rows.question: Which of the following are examples of the NATO Phonetic Alphabet?
rows.answer_c: America, Boston, Canada, Denmark

rows.question: Why do many amateurs keep a station log?
rows.answer_a: The FCC requires a log of all international contacts
rows.answer_b: The FCC requires a log of all international third-party traffic
rows.answer_c: The log provides evidence of operation needed to renew a license without retest
rows.answer_d: To help with a reply if the FCC requests information about your station

rows.question: Which of the following is required when participating in a contest on HF frequencies?
rows.answer_a: Submit a log to the contest sponsor
rows.answer_b: Send a QSL card to the stations worked, or QSL via Logbook of The World
rows.answer_c: Identify your station according to normal FCC regulations

rows.question: What is QRP operation?
rows.answer_c: Transmission using Quick Response Protocol

rows.question: Why are signal reports typically exchanged at the beginning of an HF contact?
rows.answer_a: To allow each station to operate according to conditions
rows.answer_b: To be sure the contact will count for award programs
rows.answer_c: To follow standard radiogram structure
rows.answer_d: To allow each station to calibrate their frequency display

rows.question: Which mode is normally used when sending RTTY signals via AFSK with an SSB transmitter?
rows.answer_c: CW

rows.question: What is VARA?
rows.answer_a: A low signal-to-noise digital mode used for EME (moonbounce)
rows.answer_b: A digital protocol used with Winlink
rows.answer_c: A radio direction finding system used on VHF and UHF
rows.answer_d: A DX spotting system using a network of software defined radios

rows.question: What symptoms may result from other signals interfering with a PACTOR or VARA transmission?
rows.answer_c: Failure to establish a connection between stations

rows.question: Which of the following is good practice when choosing a transmitting frequency to answer a station calling CQ using FT8?
rows.answer_a: Always call on the station’s frequency
rows.answer_b: Call on any frequency in the waterfall except the station’s frequency
rows.answer_c: Find a clear frequency during the same time slot as the calling station
rows.answer_d: Find a clear frequency during the alternate time slot to the calling station

rows.question: What is the standard sideband for JT65, JT9, FT4, or FT8 digital signal when using AFSK?
rows.answer_c: DSB

rows.question: What is the most common frequency shift for RTTY emissions in the amateur HF bands?
rows.answer_c: 425 Hz

rows.question: Which of the following is required when using FT8?
rows.answer_b: Computer time accurate to within approximately 1 second
rows.answer_c: Receiver attenuator set to -12 dB

rows.question: In what segment of the 20-meter band are most digital mode operations commonly found?
rows.answer_a: At the bottom of the slow-scan TV segment, near 14.230 MHz
rows.answer_b: At the top of the SSB phone segment, near 14.325 MHz
rows.answer_c: In the middle of the CW segment, near 14.100 MHz

rows.question: How do you join a contact between two stations using the PACTOR protocol?
rows.answer_a: Send broadcast packets containing your call sign while in MONITOR mode
rows.answer_b: Transmit a steady carrier until the PACTOR protocol times out and disconnects
rows.answer_c: Joining an existing contact is not possible, PACTOR connections are limited to two stations

rows.question: Which of the following is a way to establish contact with a digital messaging system gateway station?
rows.answer_a: Send an email to the system control operator
rows.answer_c: Respond when the station broadcasts its SSID
rows.answer_d: Transmit a connect message on the station’s published frequency

rows.question: What is the primary purpose of an Amateur Radio Emergency Data Network (AREDN) mesh network?
rows.answer_a: To provide FM repeater coverage in remote areas
rows.answer_b: To provide real time propagation data by monitoring amateur radio transmissions worldwide
rows.answer_c: To provide high-speed data services during an emergency or community event
rows.answer_d: To provide DX spotting reports to aid contesters and DXers

rows.question: Which of the following describes Winlink?
rows.answer_a: An amateur radio wireless network to send and receive email on the internet
rows.answer_c: A wireless network capable of both VHF and HF band operation

rows.question: What is another name for a Winlink Remote Message Server?
rows.answer_c: RJ-45

rows.question: What could be wrong if you cannot decode an RTTY or other FSK signal even though it is apparently tuned in properly?
rows.answer_a: The mark and space frequencies may be reversed
rows.answer_b: You may have selected the wrong baud rate
rows.answer_c: You may be listening on the wrong sideband

rows.question: Which of the following is a common location for FT8?
rows.answer_a: Anywhere in the voice portion of the band
rows.answer_b: Anywhere in the CW portion of the band
rows.answer_c: Approximately 14.074 MHz to 14.077 MHz

rows.question: How does a higher sunspot number affect HF propagation?
rows.answer_a: Higher sunspot numbers generally indicate a greater probability of good propagation at higher frequencies
rows.answer_b: Lower sunspot numbers generally indicate greater probability of sporadic E propagation
rows.answer_c: A zero sunspot number indicates that radio propagation is not possible on any band
rows.answer_d: A zero sunspot number indicates undisturbed conditions

rows.question: What effect does a sudden ionospheric disturbance have on the daytime ionospheric propagation?
rows.answer_a: It enhances propagation on all HF frequencies
rows.answer_b: It disrupts signals on lower frequencies more than those on higher frequencies
rows.answer_c: It disrupts communications via satellite more than direct communications
rows.answer_d: None, because only areas on the night side of the Earth are affected

rows.question: Approximately how long does it take the increased ultraviolet and X-ray radiation from a solar flare to affect radio propagation on Earth?
rows.answer_c: 8 minutes

rows.question: Which of the following are the least reliable bands for long-distance communications during periods of low solar activity?
rows.answer_c: 30 meters and 20 meters

rows.question: What is the solar flux index?
rows.answer_a: A measure of the highest frequency that is useful for ionospheric propagation between two points on Earth
rows.answer_b: A count of sunspots that is adjusted for solar emissions
rows.answer_c: Another name for the American sunspot number
rows.answer_d: A measure of solar radiation with a wavelength of 10.7 centimeters

rows.question: What is a geomagnetic storm?
rows.answer_a: A sudden drop in the solar flux index
rows.answer_b: A thunderstorm that affects radio propagation
rows.answer_c: Ripples in the geomagnetic force
rows.answer_d: A temporary disturbance in Earth’s geomagnetic field

rows.question: At what point in the solar cycle does the 20-meter band usually support worldwide propagation during daylight hours?
rows.answer_c: Only at the minimum point

rows.question: How can a geomagnetic storm affect HF propagation?
rows.answer_c: Improve ground wave propagation

rows.question: How can high geomagnetic activity benefit radio communications?
rows.answer_a: Creates auroras that can reflect VHF signals
rows.answer_b: Increases signal strength for HF signals passing through the polar regions
rows.answer_c: Improve HF long path propagation

rows.question: What causes HF propagation conditions to vary periodically in a 26- to 28-day cycle?
rows.answer_a: Long term oscillations in the upper atmosphere
rows.answer_b: Cyclic variation in Earth’s radiation belts
rows.answer_c: Rotation of the Sun’s surface layers around its axis
rows.answer_d: The position of the Moon in its orbit

rows.question: How long does it take a coronal mass ejection to affect radio propagation on Earth?
rows.answer_c: 4 to 8 minutes

rows.question: What does the K-index measure?
rows.answer_a: The relative position of sunspots on the surface of the Sun
rows.answer_b: The short-term stability of Earth’s geomagnetic field
rows.answer_c: The short-term stability of the Sun’s magnetic field
rows.answer_d: The solar radio flux at Boulder, Colorado

rows.question: What does the A-index measure?
rows.answer_a: The relative position of sunspots on the surface of the Sun
rows.answer_b: The amount of polarization of the Sun’s electric field
rows.answer_c: The long-term stability of Earth’s geomagnetic field
rows.answer_d: The solar radio flux at Boulder, Colorado

rows.question: How is long distance radio communication usually affected by the charged particles that reach Earth from solar coronal holes?
rows.answer_c: VHF/UHF ducting is improved

rows.question: What is a characteristic of skywave signals arriving at your location by both short-path and long-path propagation?
rows.answer_c: The signal might be cancelled causing severe attenuation
rows.answer_d: A slightly delayed echo might be heard

rows.question: What factors affect the MUF?
rows.answer_c: Solar radiation and ionospheric disturbances

rows.question: Which frequency will have the least attenuation for long-distance skip propagation?
rows.answer_c: Just below the critical frequency

rows.question: Which of the following is a way to determine current propagation on a desired band from your station?
rows.answer_a: Use a network of automated receiving stations on the internet to see where your transmissions are being received
rows.answer_c: Send a series of dots and listen for echoes

rows.question: How does the ionosphere affect radio waves with frequencies below the MUF and above the LUF?
rows.answer_a: They are refracted back to Earth
rows.answer_c: They are amplified by interaction with the ionosphere
rows.answer_d: They are refracted and trapped in the ionosphere to circle Earth

rows.question: What usually happens to radio waves with frequencies below the LUF?
rows.answer_a: They are refracted back to Earth
rows.answer_c: They are attenuated before reaching the destination
rows.answer_d: They are refracted and trapped in the ionosphere to circle Earth

rows.question: What does LUF stand for?
rows.answer_a: The Lowest Usable Frequency for communications between two specific points
rows.answer_b: The Lowest Usable Frequency for communications to any point outside a 100-mile radius
rows.answer_c: The Lowest Usable Frequency during a 24-hour period
rows.answer_d: The Lowest Usable Frequency during the past 60 minutes

rows.question: What does MUF stand for?
rows.answer_a: The Minimum Usable Frequency for communications between two points
rows.answer_b: The Maximum Usable Frequency for communications between two points
rows.answer_c: The Minimum Usable Frequency during a 24-hour period
rows.answer_d: The Maximum Usable Frequency during a 24-hour period

rows.question: What is the approximate maximum distance along the Earth’s surface normally covered in one hop using the F2 region?
rows.answer_c: 2,500 miles

rows.question: What is the approximate maximum distance along the Earth’s surface normally covered in one hop using the E region?
rows.answer_c: 2,500 miles

rows.question: What happens to HF propagation when the LUF exceeds the MUF?
rows.answer_a: Propagation via ordinary skywave communications is not possible over that path
rows.answer_b: HF communications over the path are enhanced
rows.answer_c: Double-hop propagation along the path is more common
rows.answer_d: Propagation over the path on all HF frequencies is enhanced

rows.question: Which of the following is typical of the lower HF frequencies during the summer?
rows.answer_a: Poor propagation at any time of day
rows.answer_c: Heavy distortion on signals due to photon absorption
rows.answer_d: High levels of atmospheric noise or static

rows.question: Which ionospheric region is closest to the surface of Earth?
rows.answer_c: The F1 region

rows.question: What is meant by the term “critical frequency” at a given incidence angle?
rows.answer_a: The highest frequency which is refracted back to Earth
rows.answer_b: The lowest frequency which is refracted back to Earth
rows.answer_c: The frequency at which the signal-to-noise ratio approaches unity
rows.answer_d: The frequency at which the signal-to-noise ratio is 6 dB

rows.question: Why is skip propagation via the F2 region longer than that via the other ionospheric regions?
rows.answer_c: Because it is the highest

rows.question: What does the term “critical angle” mean, as applied to radio wave propagation?
rows.answer_a: The long path azimuth of a distant station
rows.answer_b: The short path azimuth of a distant station
rows.answer_c: The lowest takeoff angle that will return a radio wave to Earth under specific ionospheric conditions
rows.answer_d: The highest takeoff angle that will return a radio wave to Earth under specific ionospheric conditions

rows.question: Why is long-distance communication on the 40-, 60-, 80-, and 160-meter bands more difficult during the day?
rows.answer_a: The F region absorbs signals at these frequencies during daylight hours
rows.answer_b: The F region is unstable during daylight hours
rows.answer_c: The D region absorbs signals at these frequencies during daylight hours
rows.answer_d: The E region is unstable during daylight hours

rows.question: What is a characteristic of HF scatter?
rows.answer_c: There are very large, sudden swings in signal strength
rows.answer_d: Scatter propagation occurs only at night

rows.question: What makes HF scatter signals often sound distorted?
rows.answer_a: The ionospheric region involved is unstable
rows.answer_b: Ground waves are absorbing much of the signal
rows.answer_c: The E region is not present
rows.answer_d: Energy is scattered into the skip zone through several different paths

rows.question: Why are HF scatter signals in the skip zone usually weak?
rows.answer_a: Only a small part of the signal energy is scattered into the skip zone
rows.answer_b: Signals are scattered from the magnetosphere, which is not a good reflector
rows.answer_c: Propagation is via ground waves, which absorb most of the signal energy
rows.answer_d: Propagation is via ducts in the F region, which absorb most of the energy

rows.question: What type of propagation allows signals to be heard in the transmitting station’s skip zone?
rows.answer_c: Chordal hop

rows.question: What is near vertical incidence skywave (NVIS) propagation?
rows.answer_b: Short distance MF or HF propagation at high elevation angles
rows.answer_c: Long path HF propagation at sunrise and sunset
rows.answer_d: Double hop propagation near the LUF

rows.question: Which ionospheric region is the most absorbent of signals below 10 MHz during daylight hours?
rows.answer_c: The E region

rows.question: What is the purpose of the notch filter found on many HF transceivers?
rows.answer_a: To restrict the transmitter voice bandwidth
rows.answer_b: To reduce interference from carriers in the receiver passband
rows.answer_c: To eliminate receiver interference from impulse noise sources
rows.answer_d: To remove interfering splatter generated by signals on adjacent frequencies

rows.question: What is the benefit of using the opposite or “reverse” sideband when receiving CW?
rows.answer_a: Interference from impulse noise will be eliminated
rows.answer_b: More stations can be accommodated within a given signal passband
rows.answer_c: It may be possible to reduce or eliminate interference from other signals
rows.answer_d: Accidental out-of-band operation can be prevented

rows.question: How does a noise blanker work?
rows.answer_b: By redirecting noise pulses into a filter capacitor
rows.answer_c: By reducing receiver gain during a noise pulse

rows.question: What is the effect on plate current of the correct setting of a vacuum-tube RF power amplifier’s TUNE control?
rows.answer_c: No change will be observed

rows.question: Why is automatic level control (ALC) used with an RF power amplifier?
rows.answer_a: To balance the transmitter audio frequency response
rows.answer_c: To prevent excessive drive

rows.question: What is the purpose of an antenna tuner?
rows.answer_a: Reduce the SWR in the feed line to the antenna
rows.answer_b: Reduce the power dissipation in the feedline to the antenna
rows.answer_c: Increase power transfer from the transmitter to the feed line

rows.question: What happens as a receiver’s noise reduction control level is increased?
rows.answer_c: CW signals may become severely attenuated
rows.answer_d: Received frequency may shift several kHz

rows.question: What is the correct adjustment for the LOAD or COUPLING control of a vacuum tube RF power amplifier?
rows.answer_b: Minimum plate current without exceeding maximum allowable grid current
rows.answer_c: Highest plate voltage while minimizing grid current
rows.answer_d: Desired power output without exceeding maximum allowable plate current

rows.question: What is the purpose of delaying RF output after activating a transmitter’s keying line to an external amplifier?
rows.answer_a: To prevent key clicks on CW
rows.answer_c: To allow time for the amplifier to switch the antenna between the transceiver and the amplifier output
rows.answer_d: To allow time for the amplifier power supply to reach operating level

rows.question: What is the function of an electronic keyer?
rows.answer_b: Automatic generation of dots and dashes for CW operation
rows.answer_c: To allow time for switching the antenna from the receiver to the transmitter
rows.answer_d: Computer interface for PSK and RTTY operation

rows.question: Why should the ALC system be inactive when transmitting AFSK data signals?
rows.answer_a: ALC will invert the modulation of the AFSK mode
rows.answer_b: The ALC action distorts the signal
rows.answer_c: When using digital modes, too much ALC activity can cause the transmitter to overheat

rows.question: Which of the following is a common use of the dual-VFO feature on a transceiver?
rows.answer_a: To allow transmitting on two frequencies at once
rows.answer_b: To permit full duplex operation -- that is, transmitting and receiving at the same time
rows.answer_c: To transmit on one frequency and listen on another
rows.answer_d: To improve frequency accuracy by allowing variable frequency output (VFO) operation

rows.question: What is the purpose of using a receive attenuator?
rows.answer_a: To prevent receiver overload from strong incoming signals
rows.answer_b: To reduce the transmitter power when driving a linear amplifier
rows.answer_c: To reduce power consumption when operating from batteries
rows.answer_d: To reduce excessive audio level on strong signals

rows.question: What item of test equipment contains horizontal and vertical channel amplifiers?
rows.answer_c: An ammeter

rows.question: Which of the following is an advantage of an oscilloscope versus a digital voltmeter?
rows.answer_b: Complex impedances can be easily measured
rows.answer_c: Greater precision

rows.question: Which of the following is the best instrument to use for checking the keying waveform of a CW transmitter?
rows.answer_c: A sidetone monitor

rows.question: What signal source is connected to the vertical input of an oscilloscope when checking the RF envelope pattern of a transmitted signal?
rows.answer_a: The local oscillator of the transmitter
rows.answer_c: The transmitter balanced mixer output
rows.answer_d: The attenuated RF output of the transmitter

rows.question: Why do voltmeters have high input impedance?
rows.answer_b: It allows for higher voltages to be safely measured
rows.answer_c: It improves the resolution of the readings
rows.answer_d: It decreases the loading on circuits being measured

rows.question: What is an advantage of a digital multimeter as compared to an analog multimeter?
rows.answer_c: Higher precision

rows.question: What signals are used to conduct a two-tone test?
rows.answer_a: Two audio signals of the same frequency shifted 90 degrees
rows.answer_c: Two swept frequency tones
rows.answer_d: Two audio frequency range square wave signals of equal amplitude

rows.question: What transmitter performance parameter does a two-tone test analyze?
rows.answer_b: Percentage of suppression of the carrier and undesired sideband for SSB
rows.answer_c: Percentage of frequency modulation

rows.question: When is an analog multimeter preferred to a digital multimeter?
rows.answer_c: When measuring the frequency of an oscillator
rows.answer_d: When adjusting circuits for maximum or minimum values

rows.question: Which of the following can be determined with a directional wattmeter?
rows.answer_c: RF interference

rows.question: Which of the following must be connected to an antenna analyzer when it is being used for SWR measurements?
rows.answer_c: Antenna and feed line

rows.question: What effect can strong signals from nearby transmitters have on an antenna analyzer?
rows.answer_a: Desensitization which can cause intermodulation products which interfere with impedance readings
rows.answer_b: Received power that interferes with SWR readings
rows.answer_c: Generation of harmonics which interfere with frequency readings

rows.question: Which of the following can be measured with an antenna analyzer?
rows.answer_c: Impedance of coaxial cable

rows.question: Which of the following might be useful in reducing RF interference to audio frequency circuits?
rows.answer_c: Forward-biased diode

rows.question: Which of the following could be a cause of interference covering a wide range of frequencies?
rows.answer_a: Not using a balun or line isolator to feed balanced antennas
rows.answer_b: Lack of rectification of the transmitter’s signal in power conductors
rows.answer_c: Arcing at a poor electrical connection
rows.answer_d: Using a balun to feed an unbalanced antenna

rows.question: What sound is heard from an audio device experiencing RF interference from a single sideband phone transmitter?
rows.answer_a: A steady hum whenever the transmitter is on the air
rows.answer_c: Distorted speech

rows.question: What sound is heard from an audio device experiencing RF interference from a CW transmitter?
rows.answer_b: A CW signal at a nearly pure audio frequency
rows.answer_c: A chirpy CW signal

rows.question: What is a possible cause of high voltages that produce RF burns?
rows.answer_a: Flat braid rather than round wire has been used for the ground wire
rows.answer_b: Insulated wire has been used for the ground wire
rows.answer_c: The ground rod is resonant
rows.answer_d: The ground wire has high impedance on that frequency

rows.question: What is a possible effect of a resonant ground connection?
rows.answer_c: High RF voltages on the enclosures of station equipment

rows.question: Why should soldered joints not be used in lightning protection ground connections?
rows.answer_a: A soldered joint will likely be destroyed by the heat of a lightning strike
rows.answer_b: Solder flux will prevent a low conductivity connection
rows.answer_c: Solder has too high a dielectric constant to provide adequate lightning protection

rows.question: Which of the following would reduce RF interference caused by common-mode current on an audio cable?
rows.answer_a: Place a ferrite choke on the cable
rows.answer_b: Connect the center conductor to the shield of all cables to short circuit the RFI signal
rows.answer_c: Ground the center conductor of the audio cable causing the interference
rows.answer_d: Add an additional insulating jacket to the cable

rows.question: How can the effects of ground loops be minimized?
rows.answer_a: Connect all ground conductors in series
rows.answer_b: Connect the AC neutral conductor to the ground wire
rows.answer_c: Avoid using lock washers and star washers when making ground connections

rows.question: What could be a symptom caused by a ground loop in your station’s audio connections?
rows.answer_a: You receive reports of “hum” on your station’s transmitted signal
rows.answer_b: The SWR reading for one or more antennas is suddenly very high
rows.answer_c: An item of station equipment starts to draw excessive amounts of current
rows.answer_d: You receive reports of harmonic interference from your station

rows.question: What technique helps to minimize RF “hot spots” in an amateur station?
rows.answer_a: Building all equipment in a metal enclosure
rows.answer_c: Bonding all equipment enclosures together
rows.answer_d: Placing low-pass filters on all feed lines

rows.question: Why must all metal enclosures of station equipment be grounded?
rows.answer_a: It prevents a blown fuse in the event of an internal short circuit
rows.answer_c: It ensures that the neutral wire is grounded
rows.answer_d: It ensures that hazardous voltages cannot appear on the chassis

rows.question: What is the purpose of a speech processor in a transceiver?
rows.answer_a: Increase the apparent loudness of transmitted voice signals
rows.answer_b: Increase transmitter bass response for more natural-sounding SSB signals
rows.answer_c: Prevent distortion of voice signals
rows.answer_d: Decrease high-frequency voice output to prevent out-of-band operation

rows.question: How does a speech processor affect a single sideband phone signal?
rows.answer_c: It reduces harmonic distortion

rows.question: What is the effect of an incorrectly adjusted speech processor?
rows.answer_c: Excessive background noise

rows.question: What does an S meter measure?
rows.answer_c: Received signal strength

rows.question: How does a signal that reads 20 dB over S9 compare to one that reads S9 on a receiver, assuming a properly calibrated S meter?
rows.answer_c: It is 20 times more powerful

rows.question: How much change in signal strength is typically represented by one S unit?
rows.answer_c: 15 dB

rows.question: How much must the power output of a transmitter be raised to change the S meter reading on a distant receiver from S8 to S9?
rows.answer_c: Approximately 4 times

rows.question: What frequency range is occupied by a 3 kHz LSB signal when the displayed carrier frequency is set to 7.178 MHz?
rows.answer_c: 7.175 MHz to 7.178 MHz

rows.question: What frequency range is occupied by a 3 kHz USB signal with the displayed carrier frequency set to 14.347 MHz?
rows.answer_c: 14.344 MHz to 14.347 MHz

rows.question: How close to the lower edge of a band’s phone segment should your displayed carrier frequency be when using 3 kHz wide LSB?
rows.answer_a: At least 3 kHz above the edge of the segment
rows.answer_b: At least 3 kHz below the edge of the segment
rows.answer_c: At least 1 kHz below the edge of the segment
rows.answer_d: At least 1 kHz above the edge of the segment

rows.question: How close to the upper edge of a band’s phone segment should your displayed carrier frequency be when using 3 kHz wide USB?
rows.answer_a: At least 3 kHz above the edge of the band
rows.answer_b: At least 3 kHz below the edge of the band
rows.answer_c: At least 1 kHz above the edge of the segment
rows.answer_d: At least 1 kHz below the edge of the segment

rows.question: What is the purpose of a capacitance hat on a mobile antenna?
rows.answer_a: To increase the power handling capacity of a whip antenna
rows.answer_c: To electrically lengthen a physically short antenna

rows.question: What is the purpose of a corona ball on an HF mobile antenna?
rows.answer_a: To narrow the operating bandwidth of the antenna
rows.answer_b: To increase the “Q” of the antenna
rows.answer_c: To reduce the chance of damage if the antenna should strike an object
rows.answer_d: To reduce RF voltage discharge from the tip of the antenna while transmitting

rows.question: Which of the following direct, fused power connections would be the best for a 100-watt HF mobile installation?
rows.answer_a: To the battery using heavy-gauge wire
rows.answer_b: To the alternator or generator using heavy-gauge wire
rows.answer_c: To the battery using insulated heavy duty balanced transmission line
rows.answer_d: To the alternator or generator using insulated heavy duty balanced transmission line

rows.question: Why should DC power for a 100-watt HF transceiver not be supplied by a vehicle’s auxiliary power socket?
rows.answer_a: The socket is not wired with an RF-shielded power cable
rows.answer_b: The socket’s wiring may be inadequate for the current drawn by the transceiver
rows.answer_c: The DC polarity of the socket is reversed from the polarity of modern HF transceivers
rows.answer_d: Drawing more than 50 watts from this socket could cause the engine to overheat

rows.question: Which of the following most limits an HF mobile installation?
rows.answer_b: The wire gauge of the DC power line to the transceiver
rows.answer_c: Efficiency of the electrically short antenna
rows.answer_d: FCC rules limiting mobile output power on the 75-meter band

rows.question: What is one disadvantage of using a shortened mobile antenna as opposed to a full-size antenna?
rows.answer_a: Short antennas are more likely to cause distortion of transmitted signals
rows.answer_b: Q of the antenna will be very low
rows.answer_c: Operating bandwidth may be very limited

rows.question: Which of the following may cause receive interference to an HF transceiver installed in a vehicle?
rows.answer_c: The control computers

rows.question: In what configuration are the individual cells in a solar panel connected together?
rows.answer_c: Bypass

rows.question: What is the approximate open-circuit voltage from a fully illuminated silicon photovoltaic cell?
rows.answer_c: 0.2 VDC

rows.question: Why should a series diode be connected between a solar panel and a storage battery that is being charged by the panel?
rows.answer_a: To prevent overload by regulating the charging voltage

rows.answer_c: Higher loss increases the accuracy of SWR measured at the input to the line
rows.answer_d: Transmission line loss does not affect the SWR measurement

rows.question: What is a characteristic of a random-wire HF antenna connected directly to the transmitter?
rows.answer_a: It must be longer than 1 wavelength
rows.answer_b: Station equipment may carry significant RF current
rows.answer_c: It produces only vertically polarized radiation
rows.answer_d: It is more effective on the lower HF bands than on the higher bands

rows.question: Which of the following is a common way to adjust the feed point impedance of an elevated quarter-wave ground-plane vertical antenna to be approximately 50 ohms?
rows.answer_c: Lengthen the radials beyond one wavelength

rows.question: Which of the following best describes the radiation pattern of a quarter-wave ground-plane vertical antenna?
rows.answer_c: Hemispherical

rows.question: What is the radiation pattern of a dipole antenna in free space in a plane containing the conductor?
rows.answer_a: It is a figure-eight at right angles to the antenna
rows.answer_b: It is a figure-eight off both ends of the antenna
rows.answer_c: It is a circle (equal radiation in all directions)
rows.answer_d: It has a pair of lobes on one side of the antenna and a single lobe on the other side

rows.question: How does antenna height affect the azimuthal radiation pattern of a horizontal dipole HF antenna at elevation angles higher than about 45 degrees?
rows.answer_a: If the antenna is too high, the pattern becomes unpredictable
rows.answer_b: Antenna height has no effect on the pattern
rows.answer_c: If the antenna is less than 1/2 wavelength high, the azimuthal pattern is almost omnidirectional
rows.answer_d: If the antenna is less than 1/2 wavelength high, radiation off the ends of the wire is eliminated

rows.question: Where should the radial wires of a ground-mounted vertical antenna system be placed?
rows.answer_a: As high as possible above the ground
rows.answer_c: On the surface or buried a few inches below the ground
rows.answer_d: At the center of the antenna

rows.question: How does the feed point impedance of a horizontal 1/2 wave dipole antenna change as the antenna height is reduced to 1/10 wavelength above ground?
rows.answer_c: It peaks at about 1/8 wavelength above ground
rows.answer_d: It is unaffected by the height above ground

rows.question: How does the feed point impedance of a 1/2 wave dipole change as the feed point is moved from the center toward the ends?
rows.answer_c: It peaks at about 1/8 wavelength from the end
rows.answer_d: It is unaffected by the location of the feed point

rows.question: Which of the following is an advantage of using a horizontally polarized as compared to a vertically polarized HF antenna?
rows.answer_c: Shorter radials

rows.question: What is the approximate length for a 1/2 wave dipole antenna cut for 14.250 MHz?
rows.answer_c: 24 feet

rows.question: What is the approximate length for a 1/2 wave dipole antenna cut for 3.550 MHz?
rows.answer_c: 132 feet

rows.question: What is the approximate length for a 1/4 wave monopole antenna cut for 28.5 MHz?
rows.answer_c: 16 feet

rows.question: Which of the following would increase the bandwidth of a Yagi antenna?
rows.answer_c: Loading coils in series with the element

rows.question: What is the approximate length of the driven element of a Yagi antenna?
rows.answer_c: 3/4 wavelength

rows.question: How do the lengths of a three-element Yagi reflector and director compare to that of the driven element?
rows.answer_a: The reflector is longer, and the director is shorter
rows.answer_b: The reflector is shorter, and the director is longer
rows.answer_c: They are all the same length
rows.answer_d: Relative length depends on the frequency of operation

rows.question: How does antenna gain in dBi compare to gain stated in dBd for the same antenna?
rows.answer_a: Gain in dBi is 2.15 dB lower
rows.answer_b: Gain in dBi is 2.15 dB higher
rows.answer_c: Gain in dBd is 1.25 dBd lower
rows.answer_d: Gain in dBd is 1.25 dBd higher

rows.question: What is the primary effect of increasing boom length and adding directors to a Yagi antenna?
rows.answer_c: Front-to-back ratio decreases

rows.question: What does “front-to-back ratio” mean in reference to a Yagi antenna?
rows.answer_a: The number of directors versus the number of reflectors
rows.answer_b: The relative position of the driven element with respect to the reflectors and directors
rows.answer_c: The power radiated in the major lobe compared to that in the opposite direction
rows.answer_d: The ratio of forward gain to dipole gain

rows.question: What is meant by the “main lobe” of a directive antenna?
rows.answer_a: The magnitude of the maximum vertical angle of radiation
rows.answer_b: The point of maximum current in a radiating antenna element
rows.answer_c: The maximum voltage standing wave point on a radiating element
rows.answer_d: The direction of maximum radiated field strength from the antenna

rows.question: In free space, how does the gain of two three-element, horizontally polarized Yagi antennas spaced vertically 1/2 wavelength apart typically compare to the gain of a single three-element Yagi?
rows.answer_c: Approximately 6 dB higher

rows.question: Which of the following can be adjusted to optimize forward gain, front-to-back ratio, or SWR bandwidth of a Yagi antenna?
rows.answer_a: The physical length of the boom
rows.answer_b: The number of elements on the boom
rows.answer_c: The spacing of each element along the boom

rows.question: What is a beta or hairpin match?
rows.answer_a: A shorted transmission line stub placed at the feed point of a Yagi antenna to provide impedance matching
rows.answer_b: A 1/4 wavelength section of 75-ohm coax in series with the feed point of a Yagi to provide impedance matching
rows.answer_c: A series capacitor selected to cancel the inductive reactance of a folded dipole antenna
rows.answer_d: A section of 300-ohm twin-lead transmission line used to match a folded dipole antenna

rows.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of using a gamma match with a Yagi antenna?
rows.answer_a: It does not require the driven element to be insulated from the boom
rows.answer_b: It does not require any inductors or capacitors
rows.answer_c: It is useful for matching multiband antennas

rows.question: Which of the following antenna types will be most effective as a near vertical incidence skywave (NVIS) antenna for short-skip communications on 40 meters during the day?
rows.answer_a: A horizontal dipole placed between 1/10 and 1/4 wavelength above the ground
rows.answer_b: A vertical antenna placed between 1/4 and 1/2 wavelength above the ground
rows.answer_c: A horizontal dipole placed at approximately 1/2 wavelength above the ground
rows.answer_d: A vertical dipole placed at approximately 1/2 wavelength above the ground

rows.question: What is the feed point impedance of an end-fed half-wave antenna?
rows.answer_c: Approximately 300 ohms

rows.question: In which direction is the maximum radiation from a VHF/UHF “halo” antenna?
rows.answer_a: Broadside to the plane of the halo
rows.answer_c: Omnidirectional in the plane of the halo
rows.answer_d: On the same side as the feed point

rows.question: What is the primary function of antenna traps?
rows.answer_c: To provide balanced feed point impedance

rows.question: What is an advantage of vertically stacking horizontally polarized Yagi antennas?
rows.answer_a: It allows quick selection of vertical or horizontal polarization
rows.answer_b: It allows simultaneous vertical and horizontal polarization
rows.answer_c: It narrows the main lobe in azimuth
rows.answer_d: It narrows the main lobe in elevation

rows.question: Which of the following is an advantage of a log-periodic antenna?
rows.answer_b: Higher gain per element than a Yagi antenna
rows.answer_c: Harmonic suppression

rows.question: Which of the following describes a log-periodic antenna?
rows.answer_a: Element length and spacing vary logarithmically along the boom
rows.answer_b: Impedance varies periodically as a function of frequency
rows.answer_c: Gain varies logarithmically as a function of frequency
rows.answer_d: SWR varies periodically as a function of boom length

rows.question: How does a “screwdriver” mobile antenna adjust its feed point impedance?
rows.answer_b: By varying the base loading inductance
rows.answer_c: By extending and retracting the whip

rows.question: What is the primary use of a Beverage antenna?
rows.answer_a: Directional receiving for MF and low HF bands
rows.answer_b: Directional transmitting for low HF bands
rows.answer_c: Portable direction finding at higher HF frequencies
rows.answer_d: Portable direction finding at lower HF frequencies

rows.question: In which direction or directions does an electrically small loop (less than 1/10 wavelength in circumference) have nulls in its radiation pattern?
rows.answer_a: In the plane of the loop
rows.answer_c: Broadside and in the plane of the loop

rows.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of multiband antennas?
rows.answer_a: They present low impedance on all design frequencies
rows.answer_b: They must be used with an antenna tuner
rows.answer_c: They must be fed with open wire line

rows.question: What is the common name of a dipole with a single central support?
rows.answer_c: Sloper
